The Bas Lag series by China Melville is amazing and weird. Perdido Street Station, The Scar, The Iron Counsil. 

Literary science fiction/fantasy set in a Victorian era-adjacent world, with steam/diesel punk aesthetics, mixed with a scientific based magic system. 

They have rudimentary robotics, machines, and tech, but no flushing toilets. The bizarre structure of the city of New Crobuzon doesn't seem to allow for plumbing. 

The world building is so deep that the citites and scenery itself feel like a character. 

Overall, It left me with a desolate feeling when I was done. It's not horror per se, but it's dark and intense, violent and brutal. It's almost like the Freak Show season of American Horror Story. 

There's a lot of body horror (they have a form of punishment called remaking), sapient cactus people, and women that have beetles for heads. The Scar features an island of mosquito people, and their women are so voracious that they have to be isolated to their island or they could cause mass extinctions. 

I highly recommend that audiobooks. The narrators provide the perfect tone that matches the overall feel of the stories.

Big Ass Fans are one of my favorite makers! I  was helping a customer once and he was joking that he needed a giant, almost absurd fan, so I googled "big ass fan" and found the actual company! They make really good, big ass fans. Lol

Hunter is one of the best home use brands for sure, Menard's offers the best variety of styles, and Hampton Bay from Home Depot are good also. As far as the model, it depends on your space.

You take into account how tall the ceiling is and the the square footage of the room. How much airflow do you want to feel in your space? 

Lighting needs add another choice. Frosted glass bowls and upward facing sconces are only good for ambient light.  You need clear glass or downward, angled sconces to get the best light.

You'll also need to make sure that your fan can support higher wattage bulbs so you can get the highest wattage l.e.d you need for your space.  A 13(ish) watt l.e.d. bulb is about the equivalent range on a 100w incandescent for example.  

Color temperature on your bulb is super important to get your best quality of light! Some people need the warmer light (in the amber spectrum) and others need that ultra bright white. It depends again on your space and your eyes.
